title: Smooth proper finite-coefficient cohomology is locally constant
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a smooth proper morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $\ell$ be a prime invertible on $S$. Put $\mathbf F_\ell=\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$. Let $F$ be a sheaf of $\mathbf F_\ell$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] which is etale locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf of a finite-dimensional $\mathbf F_\ell$-vector space [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For every integer $q\geq0$, $R^qf_*F$ is etale locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf of a finite-dimensional $\mathbf F_\ell$-vector space. Higher direct images have the convention of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. No Noetherian hypothesis on $S$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0GLI, proposition-loc-cst-torsion, specialized to the Noetherian coefficient ring F_ell; includes the non-Noetherian-base reduction.

proof.text: Convert the given module-linear constant finite-module charts into IsFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf using finite_locally_constant_module_values_iff. Inverse image preserves this property. Proper base change, the Plus homology/inverse-image comparison, and the single-functor comparison identify the restriction of the higher direct image to an affine base open with the corresponding higher direct image after base change. These are the already proved module-valued APIs in SmoothProperLocallyConstant and UpperLowerStarCoherence. Thus it suffices to prove the affine-base assertion; finite local constancy then glues by IsFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf.of_openCover.

Over an arbitrary affine base, properness gives a quasi-compact quasi-separated source. The trivial one-stratum partition makes F constructible, and boundedConstructible_singleFunctor_obj shows that F[0] has constructible cohomology. Apply compact-support constructibility to any compactification of f. Since f is proper, rightDerivedLowerShriekIsoRightDerivedLowerStar identifies this compact-support object with Rf_*F[0]. The proved constructibility comparison and the homologyRightDerivedLowerStarSingleIsoPlus comparison therefore show that G = H^q(Rf_*F[0]) is constructible.

Stalkwise invertibility of ell gives invertibility in global sections by the ringed-space unit criterion. The proved module-valued smooth-proper specialization API isIso_globalSectionsUpperStarMap_upperStar_homology_of_smooth_of_isProper, followed by bijective_cospecializationMap_of_isIso_globalSectionsUpperStarMap, makes every strict-localization cospecialization map of G bijective. This is the module-valued form of smooth proper prime-to-characteristic specialization, avoiding a detour through underlying abelian sheaves.

Apply the constructible cospecialization criterion to G over the arbitrary affine base. It supplies finite local constancy directly, so no Noetherian model or local-system descent is needed. The affine-cover reduction in step 1 proves the assertion on S. Finally finite_locally_constant_module_values_iff supplies constant finite module models; over the finite ring ULift (ZMod ell), Module.Finite and finiteness of the underlying set give the required conversions.

proof_origin.reason: Compiled proof using existing module-valued smooth proper specialization and compact-support constructibility. Generalize the constructible-topology criterion, whose proof needs no Noetherian base, and thereby omit the Noetherian approximation part of Stacks 0GLI. No unit-level route changes.

tool_uses.why: Smoothness and properness persist in the local affine reductions and after increasing the approximation stage; the unit does not separately state scheme-morphism permanence.

Identifies inverse images of constant module models with the same modules, for preserving the finite-vector-space trivializations; this generic constant-sheaf fact is not a direct-image stability assertion.

Supplies the derived module proper-exchange isomorphism for a torsion single sheaf and arbitrary base change, including Spec A -> S_j; finite-type-over-a-field coefficient packages of this unit do not cover this base.
Exactness and constant-coefficient compatibility permit taking cohomology of the derived exchange while retaining the module structure; this is a general topoi fact.
Checks qcqs hypotheses for proper schemes over the affine original and approximation bases, required by the finiteness and limit-descent theorems.
Gives finite-ring etale constructibility for the identity-open proper compactification over a qcqs base, without assuming a base field; it is a fixed-finite-coefficient finiteness tool.
Identifies stalks on a locally closed stratum and its etale neighbourhood with the original stalk, used to extract finiteness from constructible local models.
Identifies the geometric stalk of a constant finite module with its underlying finite abelian group.
Gives precisely the pointed-neighbourhood specialization isomorphisms for R^q f_*F with prime coefficients invertible on an arbitrary base.
Turns finite stalks plus the specified bijective specialization maps into finite local constancy on the Noetherian stage.
The directed finite-Z-subalgebra presentation permits choosing a cofinal tail containing ell inverse, so invertibility holds at every model stage.
Supplies the inverse-limit presentation of the affine base using finite-type-over-Z stages and affine transition maps; this generic approximation is not stated in this unit.
Descends the proper finitely presented scheme to a proper model in the chosen approximation, before imposing eventual smoothness.
Makes the already chosen finitely presented model smooth at a later stage; proper-model descent alone does not give smoothness.
Identifies the base-changed source schemes as an affine-transition inverse system with limit X, which is the hypothesis of the new local-system descent theorem.
